 Minimum wage: an increase starting December 1, 2026? What to expect 
 Minimum wage: an increase starting December 1, 2026? What to expect
 Published by
 My de Sortiraparis · Photos by
 My de Sortiraparis · Updated on November 9, 2026 at 08:28 a.m.
 The minimum wage increase could be brought forward to December 1, 2026, one month ahead of the usual January date. Amount, possible extra boost, timetable: here’s a look at the options being discussed at Matignon for workers.
 Usually, the minimum wage increase waits patiently until January 1. This year, the plan could change: the government is considering bringing the increase forward to December 1, 2026 . The proposal is at the heart of the social conference convened this Monday, November 9, 2026, at Matignon by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who is due to present his announcements at the end of the discussions. The issue affects employees across France, in Paris as well as throughout Île-de-France , where the cost of living weighs heavily on low-paid workers.
 To put the starting point in context, the minimum wage has already increased twice in 2026. It rose to €12.02 gross per hour on January 1, then to €12.31 gross per hour on June 1, equivalent to €1,867.02 gross and €1,477.93 net per month for a full-time job, according to the government website .
 Will the minimum wage rise as early as December 1, 2026?
 This is the most serious option at this stage. After several weeks of protests against the high cost of living, including the cross-sector strike on November 5, the government is looking for a quick response on purchasing power. Labor Minister Jean-Pierre Farandou said he favored an increase as early as December in an interview on TF1 on Friday, November 6.
 According to information from BFMTV reported by Orange Actu , the government is reportedly ready to approve this early increase. Why December and not November? Quite simply because November payrolls have already been finalized at most companies. As we write, nothing is official yet: the date and amount must be confirmed by Matignon.
 How much would a minimum-wage worker earn in December?
 The stated goal of the Labour Minister is to raise the minimum wage above the symbolic threshold of €1,500 net per month . That would mean at least €23 net more than today for a full-time employee, an increase of just over 1.5%.
 That still falls well short of union demands. The CFDT is calling for an extra €100 net a month, while the CGT is seeking around €150, or nearly 10% of the current amount. Around 2.2 million employees are directly affected by each increase, not counting those whose industry pay scales are brought into line with the Smic.
 Will the minimum wage rise again on January 1, 2027?
 Most likely not. An increase brought forward to December would replace the automatic increase scheduled for January 1, 2027, rather than being added to it. The precedent is recent: in late 2024, Michel Barnier’s government brought the increase forward to November 1, with a 2% rise, and the minimum wage did not change on January 1, 2025.
 Without an advance increase, the January rise would have been modest. Projections based on the latest INSEE indices put it at 0.8% to 1.6%, bringing the gross hourly minimum wage to around €12.41 to €12.51. The difference between the two scenarios therefore comes down mainly to timing and the possibility of an additional boost.

 Is a boost to the minimum wage being considered?
 The “extra boost” is the portion of the increase decided by the government beyond the statutory formula. The last one came in July 2012, in the wake of François Hollande’s election. Since then, all increases have been strictly automatic, including the 2.41% increase in June 2026.
 This time, the door is being left ajar. At the end of October, Jean-Pierre Farandou raised the possibility of a limited boost, while warning that too sharp an increase could affect employment: he said the scenario backed by the unions would cost 250,000 jobs. The exchange can be read on Vie-publique.fr . Employers, for their part, fear a shock to labor costs. Other measures are also being considered, such as providing modest-income households with some relief on their energy vouchers.
 How is the increase in the minimum wage calculated?
 Automatic increases are based on two indicators. First, the change in prices for the 20% of households with the lowest incomes, excluding tobacco, as measured by Insee . Second, half of the gain in purchasing power of the average hourly wage of blue-collar and white-collar workers. The mechanism is explained in detail on Service-Public.fr .
 During the year, a safeguard clause can also trigger an increase as soon as prices rise by more than 2% since the last adjustment. It was this clause that prompted the increase on June 1, 2026. The government also retains the option of bringing forward the date of the annual adjustment, which is precisely the possibility being considered for December.
 When will the increase in the minimum wage become official?
 The first answers are expected as soon as Sébastien Lecornu speaks after the social conference. The increase will then have to be set out in a text published in the Official Journal . Under the usual schedule, the expert group on the minimum wage issues its opinion in late November and the decree is published in mid-December: an increase from December 1 would mean speeding up the process.
 Employees do not need to take any action: the increase is applied automatically to their pay slips for hours worked from the date it takes effect. Apprentices, whose pay is calculated as a percentage of the Smic, also benefit. The official amounts will be published on Service-Public.fr and on the Labor Ministry website .
 In the meantime, you can find all the details of the latest increase in our article Minimum wage increase, start of the sales, baccalaureate exams: what’s changing in June 2026 , as well as our roundup of what changed in France and Île-de-France in January 2026 . And if you want to enjoy the capital without breaking the bank, our guide to free and affordable things to do in Paris on a budget is worth keeping handy.
